data.body:
The completion verifier refused this close on AC7/AC8, and it was right in a way I did not expect: I had ticked both boxes pointing at `test_a_marker_with_a_reason_admits_a_new_mechanism`, which drives `evaluate()` with a synthetic `lock` key. That proves the admission RULE but never exercises marker HARVESTING off a real tree, so neither non-def-line placement (filename-glob head window, YAML step line) had any coverage at all.

Writing the two tests found a REAL BUG, not just a coverage hole. `parse_marker` split its body with `split(None, 2)`, so the NAME was assumed to be one whitespace-free token. A workflow step is named for its `- name:` text — or, when unnamed, for its `run:` snippet — so its name routinely contains spaces: `.github/workflows/x.yml::seeded step`, `...::pytest -q tests`. The marker for such a step harvested under a TRUNCATED key (`...::seeded`), so the step stayed unjustified and the gate reported it as new. Net effect: the YAML-step kind — 226 of the 257 ci_gate entries — could NEVER be justified by the marker idiom the gate tells you to use.

Fix: the reason now begins at the first separator with whitespace on BOTH sides, so a name may contain spaces; `::` inside a name is untouched because it carries no whitespace. Extracted as `_split_name_reason`, keeping the old two-token reading (including the leading-separator strip) as the no-separator fallback, so a blank reason is still the error it was.

Evidence: AC8's test seen RED against the old parser with the exact truncation in the failure message, GREEN after. Mutation-tested both new tests — removing the head-window bound kills the AC7 test; dropping the required trailing whitespace from the separator kills the flag-name test (I added that third case precisely because the first two survived that mutant). 31/31 in the file, live ratchet unchanged at active=681 new=0, lint + typecheck + complexity green. No regression risk to existing justifications: there are zero live markers in the tree today — all ten hits are docs and templates.
